overview.body:
# How we would build Plans

**This is a Plan, written before there is any Plan feature.** Everything below is proposed. No code described here as new exists, and no decision in it has been agreed. The stories it serves are under [Plans: agree how to build before building](urn:change-saga:change-saga:feature:plan-reviews).

## What we are building

[A Plan is what you will do; a Review is what you did](annotation:what-is). The two share a slide deck with an essay, per-slide decisions, comments, and a reading surface. They differ in when they are written and what they answer to: a Plan comes before the code and answers to stories, while a Review comes at the pull request and answers to every changed line.

[A Plan sits between the stories and the code](annotation:chain). Stories say what a person should be able to do. A Review explains what a pull request did. Nothing today carries a reviewable account of how we intend to do it, so that discussion happens out of band or not at all. A Plan does not replace the [work plan](urn:change-saga:change-saga:feature:work-planning), which divides work into waves, and it never becomes living documentation: an implementation deck says what is, and a Plan says what was intended.

## What the trial showed

This deck is also the experiment. [Every container that exists today gets something wrong](annotation:trial):

| Container | Result of trying it |
| --- | --- |
| UX deck (used here) | Published through `add-slide` with an SVG rendered elsewhere, because `apply-slide` refuses an Item with no evidence. Reads as user flows. No decisions or comments. |
| Implementation deck | Refused without exact code evidence on every Item, and its Technical section promises current code. |
| Review, in a scratch copy | `review create` on a code-free branch gave working decisions and comments, with coverage of 0 of 0 lines. The first code commit made it report 0 of 1 lines explained. |
| Feature design chapter | Prose only, no slides, and `feature deliver` refuses to move it. |

The scratch Review is the most important result: the review machinery almost holds a Plan already. What it lacks is a way to say that this review has no diff.

## Data model

[A Plan is a review record with no diff](annotation:model). `internal/saga/review.go` defines `ReviewManifest`, which requires a `base`, and `review.schema.json` requires it too. The proposal adds:

| Addition | On | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `kind: "plan"` | `review.json` | Marks a Plan. `base`, `head`, `pull_request` and `merged` do not apply. |
| `closed: {state, reason, delivered_by, closed_at}` | Plan's `review.json` | How it ended. Freezes it, as `merged` freezes a review. |
| `delivers: [plan id]` | Pull request's `review.json` | Which Plan a review delivers. |
| Relation type `plans` | Requirements relations | Links a Plan to a story with a pinned revision. |

Approvals and comments need no schema change: they already target slide and Item URNs and carry a commit.

[A Plan links to stories, not to its feature](annotation:story-link), because `feature deliver` keeps story URNs and deletes the Roadmap feature. A pinned relation also gives us stale reporting and `relation repin` without new machinery, and `internal/cli/feature_deliver.go` already moves relations with their feature.

## Storage: a review on disk, separate in memory

[We recommend storing a Plan as a review and loading it apart from reviews](annotation:storage). On disk it is `___reviews/ID.review/` with a `kind`, so its URN stays `urn:change-saga:SAGA:review:ID` and everything keyed on a review target keeps working. In memory, `loadReviews` sorts it into a new `document.Plans`.

That split matters because `document.Reviews` is used [71 times across 30 non-test Go files](annotation:reads), and code such as `internal/server/relatedreviews.go`, `internal/cli/status_grammar.go` and `internal/cli/stale_repair.go` assumes a pull request's range. With one slice, every use would have to remember to filter. With two, code sees a Plan only by asking. A sibling `___plans/` directory is equally safe, but costs a reserved name in `knownReservedDirectory`, a new URN kind beside `ReviewIDOf`, and a new command noun.

## CLI grammar

[Four additions; the rest already exists](annotation:cli). `review create --kind plan`, relation type `plans`, `review create --delivers`, and `review close` are new. `apply-slide --review`, `deck overview --review`, `visual-qa --review`, `review comment` and `review approve` all apply as they are.

[The word itself is the catch](annotation:noun). `change-saga plan` already manages work-plan waves in `internal/workplan`, and `feature set-plan` writes each feature's `plan.json`. That collision is why Plans hang off `review` rather than getting their own noun, and it is why the name is an open question.

## Reader

[A Plan opens on the existing review page, minus what needs a diff](annotation:reader). `internal/server/server.go` registers the routes under `/reviews/{id}`. Coverage, Item diffs, code, file diffs and line threads all read a range and are absent for a Plan. The page itself, visuals, annotations, feedback, decisions and comments apply unchanged. `reviewPage` in `internal/server/reviews.go` adds a banner saying that nothing here is built. `makeReviewsNav` in `appnav.go` and `reviewsDirectory` in `directories.go` list Plans on the Review side of the header, and `apppages.go` links them from the feature page.

## Decisions

[A decision on a Plan goes stale when its slide changes](annotation:decisions). `currency` in `internal/reviewstate/reviewstate.go` already compares the slide digest a decision recorded, then checks any code the slide's Items cite. A slide that cites no code has nothing further to check. The only obstacle is `ResolveRange`, which demands a merge-base with a base a Plan does not have, so a Plan resolves its head alone. `Build` also skips coverage and landing detection for one.

[The tool never declares a Plan approved](annotation:verdict). This follows SPEC section 8, "the format records; teams decide", and it is a real product question whether teams need more than that before starting work.

## Comparing what we said with what we did

[A Review accounts for its Plan the way it accounts for lines](annotation:said-did). A review Item's `record` field already opens a record beside the change, so an Item can name the Plan slide it delivers. `validReviewRecordReference` in `internal/saga/slides.go` needs to accept a review-scoped slide URN to allow it. A departure is an ordinary callout on the Review's slide. `review list` then reports which Plan slides nothing accounts for, which Review slides account for none, and the reasons recorded.

[This is an omission check, not proof](annotation:not-proof), in the same sense as coverage. A person still decides whether a slide was really delivered. It only reports, so it can never block a merge. How far each story got comes from the criteria's implementation evidence through `query traceability`, which this does not duplicate.

## Lifecycle

[A Plan ends by decision, not by a merge](annotation:lifecycle). `repin` freezes a review when its change lands, through `WriteFrozen` in `internal/reviewstore/reviewstore.go`, but a Plan delivered in phases has no single merge. `review close` records `shipped`, naming its Reviews, or `abandoned`, with a required reason. Either freezes the Plan, reusing the checks that make `Record` and `Comment` refuse a merged review. Closing changes no story and no Roadmap status.

[Keeping abandoned Plans is a recommendation, not a settled answer](annotation:keep), since it pulls against keeping the Saga as current state.

## Phases

[Four phases, each useful without the next](annotation:phases):

1. **Read.** A Plan exists: schema, loader split, `review create --kind plan`, and a page with a banner.
2. **Discuss.** Decisions and comments with no range; coverage and diff surfaces hidden; Plans listed.
3. **Connect.** The `plans` relation, `--delivers`, links from Roadmap, feature and story pages, and the comparison.
4. **Close and teach.** `review close`, delivery behaviour, SPEC section 8, and the skill. [SKILL.md tells agents to author Saga content near completion](annotation:timing), so a Plan needs its own route there.

## Risks and decisions

[The largest risks are leaks into pull-request code and Plans nobody closes](annotation:risks). The separate slice limits the first. A report in `status` limits the second without adding a gate. Plans stay optional and report-only throughout. A strict older reader refuses a Saga that holds a Plan, as with earlier additive fields, so readers must be upgraded before writing one.

Before phase 1, someone has to answer [five questions](annotation:questions): the name, whether this augments Rich visual review or stands alone, how many Reviews one Plan may have, what counts as agreed, and what happens to a closed Plan.
